why: IMAGE-SCRIPT-MATCH-1 (2026-11-14: support follows the Microsoft migration guide that the drift check watches, because the product is built on that guide): Microsoft lists the Linux releases that support NVMe. The scan holds a Linux machine whose release is not on this list from v6 and v7 (linux-release-not-on-nvme-list), and v5 stays; an unknown release is a warning (linux-release-nvme-not-read). Each row is one bullet of the page's section, in its order: distroId is the os-release ID the release reader gives (ConvertTo-VmfDistroId, Get-VmfImageRelease), major and minor the release, and andNewer means every later minor release of the same major (the page gives each major its own row). A null minor is every minor release of the major. NvmeLinuxRelease.Tests.ps1 fails when the pinned page and these rows differ, so a change on the page cannot pass without a change here. Azure Linux 3.0 is on the page, and data/supported-images.json refuses its image (AZURE-LINUX-3-SUPPORT-1). SLES-for-SAP is on the page, and the scan refuses SAP images (sap-needs-a-certified-size).
